chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from a number of our companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no cutting (of the hand) for the one who steals a cloak, and there is no cutting for the one who steals dirhams from the man's garment.

key_terms.قَطع: Cutting (amputation of the hand as a hadd punishment for theft)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hand amputation for stealing a cloak or dirhams from clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith from *al-Istibsar* clarifies the boundaries of the hadd punishment for theft by excluding specific scenarios—such as stealing a cloak or dirhams from clothing—from the full amputation ruling, likely due to differences in value or method of concealment. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on precise definitions of 'theft' (sariqah) and the conditions required for the application of corporal punishment, distinguishing between minor takings and those warranting the hadd.
